To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the assembly of the chloroplastic ATP synthase subcomplex CF1 relies on a translatory feedback loop that ensures a precise stoichiometry of its subunits.
the stoichiometry of the chloroplast ATP synthases is ensured by translational regulations that are intertwined and that involve both nuclear‐ and chloroplast‐encoded proteins.

the stoichiometry of the chloroplast ATP synthases is achieved through a feedback loop that operates along the assembly pathway, and relies on a translatory regulation of the subunit β and α, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of translation of chloroplast proteins, which is crucial in the biogenesis and assembly of the chlorophyll‐protein complexes.
the molecular mechanisms ensuring the stoichiometric assembly of the CF1 sector of chloroplast ATPases, a process that is of fundamental importance for the energy metabolism of the chloroplast.
the mechanisms of translation control in the chloroplast, and how these control mechanisms contribute to the assembly of a complex enzyme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the stoichiometry of subunits α, β and γ in chloroplast H+‐ATPA synthase is ensured by a translational regulatory loop, in which the assembly of one subunit is required for the translation of the next.

the stoichiometry of the chloroplast ATP synthetase is achieved by an intertwined translational regulation, in which the expression of each of the subunits is controlled by the assembly of its neighbouring subunits.
the stoichiometric assembly of the CF1 sector relies on the concerted action of two translational feedback loops.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

subunit β, by assembling with subunit α, is released from a negative translational feedback loop, and then, by assembling with γ, stimulates translation of subunit γ, which, in turn, is required for the sustained translation of subunit δ, the last to be assembled.

the stoichiometry of subunits is set in a two‐step process, first at the level of the chloroplast genome by translation initiation of γ, followed by a second step of feedback regulation of subunit β and α translation.
the assembly of chloroplast H+‐ATPiase subunits is regulated by a translational feedback circuitry that is unique among the biogenesis of organellar complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stoichiometry of the (C)F0F1 complex is set by the coordinated expression of nucleus‐ and chloroplast‐encoded genes.

the stoichiometry of the chloroplast F1 sector is set at two levels: at the transcriptional level, where the expression of the γ gene is required to sustain translation of the β gene, and at the translational level, where assembly of α3β3 complexes releases the translational repression of subunit β and stimulates that of subunit α.
translational regulation is an important component of the assembly of chloroplast CF1 and, more generally, of the biogenesis of chloroplast proteins.
